items.followUp: Draw a flowchart to calculate the perimeter of a rectangle.

rubric.why: The flowchart must obtain the rectangle's dimensions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing both dimensions as inputs.

rubric.why: The flowchart must calculate and present the area.
rubric.description: Calculate area = length × width and display the result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the calculation and output step.

modelAnswer: Draw an oval labelled Start.
Draw an input/output parallelogram labelled Input length (L) and width (W).
Draw a process rectangle labelled Area (A) = L × W.
Draw an input/output parallelogram labelled Display A.
Draw an oval labelled Stop and connect all symbols with arrows in order.

items.followUp: Name one software application that can be used to edit HTML code.

rubric.why: A webpage is created using software for writing or editing webpage code.
rubric.description: Identify an HTML editor or webpage-authoring application.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for naming a suitable editor, such as Notepad.

modelAnswer: An HTML editor, such as Notepad, is needed to create a webpage.

items.followUp: Convert (255)₁₀ into the hexadecimal number system.

rubric.why: Repeated division by 16 gives the hexadecimal digits as remainders.
rubric.description: Show correct division by 16 and remainders.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct division/remainder method.

rubric.why: The final hexadecimal number is formed by reading the remainders from bottom to top.

modelAnswer: 4350 ÷ 16 = 271 remainder 14 = E.
271 ÷ 16 = 16 remainder 15 = F.
16 ÷ 16 = 1 remainder 0.
1 ÷ 16 = 0 remainder 1.
Reading the remainders from bottom to top: (69610)₁₀ = (10FEA)₁₆.

items.followUp: State the identity laws for OR and AND in Boolean algebra.

rubric.why: The OR identity law states that OR with 0 leaves the variable unchanged.
The AND identity law states that AND with 1 leaves the variable unchanged.

modelAnswer: OR identity law: A + 0 = A.
AND identity law: A · 1 = A.

items.followUp: What happens when a plug-and-play device is connected to a computer?

rubric.why: The computer detects or recognizes the device automatically.
rubric.description: Explain that the computer automatically detects or recognizes the device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for automatic detection or recognition.

rubric.why: The device is set up for use with little or no manual configuration.
rubric.description: Explain that the device is configured or made ready for use with little or no manual setup.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for automatic setup/configuration or readiness to use.

modelAnswer: A plug-and-play device is automatically detected and recognized by the computer when connected.
The operating system configures it, so it can be used with little or no manual setup.

items.followUp: Explain a truth table and give an example for an OR gate.

rubric.why: A truth table records the output for every possible combination of inputs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it shows outputs for all possible input combinations.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates how the truth table works.
rubric.description: Give a correct example truth table, such as for an AND gate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct gate example and its input-output values.

modelAnswer: A truth table is a table that shows the output of a logic gate for every possible combination of its inputs.
Example: AND gate.
A | B | Output

items.followUp: Write two ways to make a password stronger.

rubric.why: A password should be sufficiently long or difficult for others to guess.
rubric.description: Give one characteristic that makes a password difficult to guess.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid characteristic, such as length or difficulty to guess.

rubric.why: Using a mixture of character types, and avoiding personal information, improves password security.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second valid characteristic, such as mixing character types or avoiding personal information.

modelAnswer: A good password should be long and difficult to guess.
It should combine uppercase and lowercase letters with numbers or special characters, and should not use easily guessed personal information.

items.followUp: What is file sharing, and how can it help people work together?

rubric.why: Application sharing involves making an application available to others over a network.
rubric.description: Explain that an application is shared with other users, typically over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the shared application and network-based access.

rubric.why: The purpose is to let other users access, view, or use the application together.
rubric.description: Describe what other users can do through application sharing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that users can access/use the application or collaborate through it.

modelAnswer: Application sharing is making a software application available to other users over a network.
The users can access or use the shared application, allowing them to work together.
